summary: Private restore exceeded customer maintenance window (restore in-place ran longer than planned)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer attempted an in-place restore of a Redwood Private deployment during an approved maintenance window.
- Restore workflow exceeded the remaining window due to longer-than-expected Postgres recovery + artifact restore time, and the customer requested guidance to (a) improve predictability and (b) add clearer pre-flight checks to Redwood docs.

Impact
- Writes were blocked in maintenance mode for longer than planned; customer reverted to partial service enablement before full validation completed.
- No data loss reported. Customer concern is operational risk: inability to confidently meet internal change-management windows.

Customer context
- Helix Financial Software (Private, regulated workload).
- Maintenance windows are tightly controlled (customer indicated 60–90 minutes typical, with hard stop due to downstream dependencies).

What happened (customer provided)
- Restore was executed per draft runbook. They enabled maintenance mode, restored DB from backup, restored object/artifact bundle, then ran smoke tests.
- Timeline (approx):
  - T+0: Entered maintenance mode
  - T+10m: Started DB restore
  - T+55m: DB restore still running (WAL replay slower than expected)
  - T+75m: Artifact restore started; object storage throughput lower than expected
  - T+95m: Customer hit window limit; exited maintenance mode with a plan to retry outside hours

Signals / logs (snippets)
- rw-private-dr output:
  - "restore execute: step postgres-recover ... replaying WAL segments"
  - "restore execute: step artifacts-restore ... copying bundle" 
- Control plane observed in maintenance mode longer than usual; customer asked if there is a supported way to estimate restore duration before entering maintenance mode.

Support/SRE triage notes
- No indication of a product bug; behavior consistent with:
  1) Postgres PITR/WAL replay time depending on WAL volume + IOPS
  2) Object storage throughput / endpoint bandwidth constraints
  3) Limited parallelism to avoid DB contention during recovery
- The runbook currently assumes operators have already validated backup integrity, throughput, and recovery time assumptions. Customer feedback: these checks are not explicit or easy to follow.

Troubleshooting performed / guidance provided
1) Recommend running a "restore plan" (dry-run) and collecting estimates BEFORE maintenance mode
- Command:
  - rw-private-dr restore plan --from s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/<backup-id> --cluster <name>
- Ask customer to capture:
  - Reported backup contents, sizes, and expected restore steps
  - Any warnings about missing WAL segments / PITR prerequisites

2) Pre-flight checks to perform outside the window (recommended)
- Backup verification:
  - rw-private-dr backup verify --from s3://<bucket>/<prefix>/<backup-id>
  - Confirm checksums, encryption settings, and that the backup includes the expected components.
- Storage throughput sanity test (customer-run):
  - Measure effective throughput from restore runner pod/node to the backup bucket endpoint (esp. if using VPC endpoints).
  - Validate that throttling is not present (cloud metrics on bucket + VPC endpoint).
- DB recovery readiness:
  - Confirm WAL archiving was enabled and continuous for the desired PITR window.
  - Confirm target restore point is close enough (large WAL replay window can dominate restore time).

3) Restore execution suggestions to improve predictability
- Prefer restoring to a new cluster for drills where possible (allows measuring end-to-end time without production write downtime), then cutover.
- If in-place restore is required:
  - Start maintenance mode only after all artifacts are staged and connectivity/IAM checks pass.
  - Ensure restore job has adequate CPU/memory and that node has sufficient ephemeral storage for unpacking bundles.
  - Confirm no competing heavy jobs are scheduled during the restore window.

4) Observability / evidence capture
- Provided customer with metrics to track during drill (backup age, restore step durations, last successful backup).
- Asked customer to share restore job logs and durations per step for tuning recommendations.

Customer request (docs)
- Customer requested clearer operator documentation covering:
  - How to estimate restore time before entering maintenance mode
  - Minimum recommended throughput/IOPS guidelines (or an explicit “restore time is dominated by X/Y” explanation)
  - A concise “pre-flight checklist” section that can be attached to change requests

Resolution
- Support/SRE provided a pre-flight checklist and recommended switching to a restore-to-new-cluster drill for time estimation, then performing in-place restore only when prerequisites are confirmed.
- Customer confirmed they can schedule a longer window for the next drill and will run restore plan + throughput checks ahead of time.

Follow-ups
- Internal: create/update docs to add a first-class pre-flight checklist and make restore duration drivers explicit.
- Internal: consider adding a "maintenance-mode start" guardrail in tooling docs (don’t enter maintenance mode until restore plan/verify passes and artifacts are accessible).

Attachments
- Customer-provided timestamps and excerpted logs included in comments.
comments:
2025-12-09 09:14 (Markus Klein, reporter)
Customer (Helix) attempted restore in-place during a 90m window and ran out of time. Asking for immediate guidance + requesting clearer docs on pre-flight checks / time estimates. Looping in SRE for drill practices.

2025-12-09 10:02 (Rafael Mendes, assignee)
Initial hypothesis: not a functional failure, but runtime exceeded window due to WAL replay and/or object storage throughput. Requesting: restore job logs, backup size, whether PITR was used, and storage target (S3 with VPC endpoint? cross-account KMS?).

2025-12-09 12:20 (Customer via Support summary)
- Backup location: S3 bucket in same account, accessed via VPC endpoint.
- Restore used PITR to 2025-12-08T23:00Z.
- Backup bundle size: ~620GB total (artifacts + logs retention included).
- Observed S3 download throughput ~80–120MB/s from restore pod.
- They entered maintenance mode before running any plan/verify step.
- Request: “We need a checklist we can run BEFORE we pull the maintenance lever.”

2025-12-09 13:05 (Rafael Mendes)
Provided guidance:
1) Run `rw-private-dr restore plan` and `backup verify` outside window.
2) Measure throughput from the same node pool that will run restore jobs.
3) For predictable windows, do a restore-to-new-cluster drill to measure end-to-end time without impacting prod, then schedule an in-place restore window with buffer.
Also shared that PITR distance (WAL volume) is often the dominant factor; recommend restoring closer to failure point if possible.

2025-12-10 08:41 (Allison Grant)
If they can share restore step durations, we can compare to our SRE targets and confirm whether they’re hitting throttling. Also: make sure they’re on the observability pack version that includes restore step annotations (see observability-pack/pr_237).

2025-12-10 10:18 (Customer via Support summary)
Acknowledged. They will:
- Re-run with a longer window.
- Run plan/verify first.
- Exclude non-essential log archives from the restore bundle for the next drill.
They reiterated docs gap: pre-flight list and guidance on sizing/throughput needed to hit RTO.

2025-12-11 16:02 (Rafael Mendes)
Captured requested doc additions for Eng Private + Docs:
- Add “Pre-flight checklist” to restore runbook (plan/verify, artifact accessibility, throughput check, WAL/PITR readiness).
- Add explicit note: do not enter maintenance mode until plan/verify passes.
- Add section on restore-time drivers (WAL replay, storage throughput, decompression/ephemeral disk).
Markus: please confirm if Helix wants a reviewed checklist they can attach to their change request template.

2025-12-12 09:27 (Markus Klein)
Confirmed: Helix wants a single-page pre-flight checklist suitable for change management. I’ll work with Docs on a customer-friendly version; SRE guidance above unblocked the immediate drill planning.

2025-12-12 11:05 (Rafael Mendes)
Marking Resolved (guidance delivered + next steps agreed). Re-open if next drill fails to meet target RTO after pre-flight checks.
